/033-117574.desc: Event Details $65-75 per class Classes offered (scout can choose up to TWO per week): Citizenship in the Community Citizenship in the Nation Citizenship in the World Communication Emergency Preparedness Environmental Science First Aid Personal Fitness Swimming Trail to Eagle has been a long running evening-only program at Camp Trask. The merit badge program is designed to assist your scout in completing the merit badge(s) they have chosen, with prerequisites assigned to each merit badge. Each class day is 1hr and 15min and includes review of the scout workbook, the work he/she has completed, lectures that pertain to the requirements, and study time in which the scout can ask questions and work on requirements in his packet. Please note that some classes may assign homework if the instructor feels more work is needed to appropriately complete the merit badge requirements. Scouts can sign up for 2 merit badges each week, 1 per each time period. The Trask Merit Badge Program runs for UP TO 4 Days. Monday thru Wednesday is the normal class Schedule 5:30 or 7:15 start times, in which most badges can be completed if all prerequisites, packet work, and counselor reviews are done. Thursday is a makeup day (at the discretion of the counselor) at which time all scheduled session start at 5:00 and end at 7:00. Please note this does not mean you have to be there at 5:00 but the Thursday session is available and open to your scout to walk in and complete his merit badge. If a scout needs more time (for example, some requirements are time sensitive to be done over 7-30 days), we will arrange a session at a later date to complete the merit badge. /053-2026Camporee.desc: Event Details 2026 Los Padres Council Camporee Two Districts. One Camporee. Endless Adventure! November 13–15, 2026 Larsen Meadow at Rancho Alegre Registration Deadline: November 8, 2026, at 11:59 PM Two Districts, One Unforgettable Adventure! Something exciting is happening at Camporee this year! For the first time, the Cuesta and Pacific Coast Districts are joining forces for one incredible Los Padres Council-wide Camporee! We're bringing Scouts together from across the council for a weekend filled with adventure, friendly competition, teamwork, outdoor skills, and unforgettable Scouting traditions. Imagine patrols cheering each other on, the aroma of Dutch oven cooking, creative gateways welcoming visitors to campsites, and Scouts gathering around a crackling evening campfire. That's the magic of Camporee! Whether you're a seasoned camper or attending your very first Camporee, this is your opportunity to put your skills to the test, strengthen your patrol, make new friends, and experience Scouting at its best. Camporee Highlights Get your patrol ready to show what you've got! Scout Skills Challenges: Test your knowledge, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a variety of competitions and activities. Campsite Inspections: Show off your patrol's organization, preparedness, and camping skills. Uniform Inspections: Demonstrate your Scout spirit and pride. Gateway Inspections: Put your unit's creativity and pioneering skills on display! Dutch Oven Cooking Competition: Break out your favorite recipes, fire up those coals, and compete for Camporee bragging rights and prizes! Campfire & Awards Ceremony: Gather with fellow Scouts to celebrate the weekend and recognize outstanding patrols and units. Plan out those amazing skits, run-ons, and songs! Your Camporee Weekend Friday, November 13 – Let the Adventure Begin! Arrival: After 5:00 PM Arrive at Larsen Meadow, check in, and head to your assigned campsite. Set up your tents, organize your patrol cooking area, and prepare for a fun-filled weekend. Dinner is on us Friday night! We'll provide a hot dog dinner so you can concentrate on getting camp set up instead of worrying about cooking after a long day. Saturday, November 14 – Adventure, Challenges & Competition! Start your morning with uniform inspections before hiking up to the main camp at Rancho Alegre for a full day of activities and Scouting challenges. Pack your daypack! You'll need to carry everything you need for the day, including: Water and refillable water bottle Sunscreen and hat Snacks and a packed lunch Comfortable hiking shoes Any other personal essentials After a day of adventure, return to Larsen Meadow for dinner. Units may prepare their own meal or enjoy our optional catered BBQ dinner from Country Meat Market. Then gather around the campfire for an evening of Scouting spirit, fellowship, and our Camporee awards ceremony! Sunday, November 15 – Until Next Time! Departure: After 7:00 AM Enjoy one final morning at camp, prepare breakfast with your patrol, break down your campsite, and head home with new friendships, stronger patrols, and memories that will last long after the tents are packed away. Optional Saturday Night BBQ Dinner $23.00 per person After a full day of activities, why not treat yourself to a delicious BBQ dinner catered by Country Meat Market? Entrées Grilled tri-tip with dry-rub seasoning Juicy grilled BBQ chicken with house BBQ sauce Salads & Sides Fresh fruit salad Country potato salad Famous vegetarian baked beans Green salad with ranch and balsamic vinaigrette dressings Bread & Condiments Homemade garlic bread Fresh-made salsa Creamy horseradish This catered meal is optional and must be purchased separately from Camporee registration. Please note: Saturday dinner availability cannot be guaranteed for registrations received after November 1, 2026. Registration Fees Register early and save!
